architecture_summary: Static dashboard with many client-rendered HTML pages and a generated data.js bundle. refresh.sh assembles local Hermes files into data.js, and publish.sh commits/pushes the result to GitHub. Trust boundary is weak: local private state is serialized into a public client bundle and rendered directly in browser pages.

infrastructure_surface.secret_management: local env vars serialized into generated client bundle

findings.title: Public dashboard bundle exposes private local state
findings.category: Secrets / OWASP A01 / OWASP A02 / OWASP A05
findings.description: The build pipeline serializes local Hermes memory, raw config, raw env content, credential inventory, reports, sessions, and other private state into data.js for client-side rendering. This is not server-side protected; it is shipped to the browser as static content.
exploit_scenario: 1. An attacker requests the public bundle from GitHub Pages or the repo raw URL.
2. They read data.js directly without authentication.
3. They extract user profile details, agent memory, config structure, integration status, report contents, skill contents, and operational metadata.
4. They use the exposed environment and architecture details to target accounts, social-engineer the operator, or pivot into other systems.
findings.impact: Direct information disclosure of personal data, operational internals, prompts, local file paths, and security-sensitive configuration. This materially lowers the cost of follow-on attacks.
findings.recommendation: Stop publishing raw local state into data.js. Move sensitive data to a private backend, publish a sanitized allowlist only, and remove config/env/memory/report dumps from client output entirely.

findings.title: Secret redaction is broken; most secret material remains visible
findings.description: refresh.sh masks only the first four characters of env values, leaving the rest of each secret intact in env_raw. The published bundle also exposes credential labels and integration status, making the leaked material easier to interpret.
exploit_scenario: 1. An attacker downloads data.js from the public repo or site.
2. They inspect env_raw and recover nearly complete token values and provider mappings.
3. They combine the leaked remainder with provider-specific formats and labels to identify which credentials to target first.
4. They attempt token abuse, account recovery, or provider-specific phishing using the exposed metadata.
findings.impact: Substantial secret leakage. Even when a value is partially obscured, enough remains to expose structure, issuer, and most of the token body.
findings.recommendation: Never publish env-derived values to the client. If a diagnostic view is absolutely required, replace each secret with a fixed placeholder like <redacted> and publish only a boolean presence flag.

supply_chain_summary.notes: No package manifests or lockfiles detected in scope; supply-chain scan limited to remote scripts/CDNs in static HTML.
